summary: gloggo impersonates glogg logger and gates a hidden payload through unrelated `file-type-detector` dependency at require time
details: Package presents itself as the `glogg` logger (README links to gulpjs/gloggo, LICENSE credits Blaine Bublitz and Contra) but is republished under an unrelated author (Blockvora Team <team@blockvora.com>). package.json adds an unrelated dependency `file-type-detector`. On `require('gloggo')`, index.js invokes `sigcheck.isSign('favorite', 'gloggo', 12259)` — passing package-identifying constants as an activation key to a foreign dependency whose stated purpose has no relation to logging — and, when the call returns truthy, chains into `require('./log')`. The `./log` module is not present in this tarball; the executed code path therefore resolves through the `file-type-detector` dependency at library load time. Combined with the identity impersonation of a well-known logger, this is the trojanized-clone shape: a legitimate package's source copied verbatim with one foreign-dep activation call added to smuggle in a downstream payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
